name: Civil Engineering & Construction
shortSummary: Roads, buildings, earthworks, drainage and erosion control.
summary: Design and construction of roads, buildings and civil works, from earthworks to finished surfaces.

intro: Civil engineering is where Sato began. We design and build the infrastructure that institutions and communities depend on, and we manage every stage, from site preparation to handover.
Our own plant and workshop mean we mobilise without waiting on hired equipment, and keep control of quality and programme on site.
Civil work is the structure everything else is fixed to. On most Sato contracts it arrives with an electrical and a mechanical package attached, and it is planned as one programme rather than three.
items: Asphaltic concrete road construction and road rehabilitation
Pavement design, construction and repair, including heavy-duty terminal pavements
Earthworks: grading, laterite filling, sub-base compaction
Drainage systems, kerbs, culverts and walkways
Building construction: academic, administrative, laboratory, residential and office buildings
Renovation and conversion of existing buildings

intro: What we deliver under this discipline, whether it is the whole contract or one package of a larger scheme.

groups.heading: Roads and pavements
description: Asphaltic concrete carriageways, heavy-duty terminal pavements, kerbs and walkways, built new or rehabilitated in place. The drainage that decides how long a surface lasts is designed with it, not after it.

groups.heading: Buildings
description: Academic, administrative, laboratory, residential and office buildings, from foundations to fit-out, and the conversion or renovation of buildings already in use.

groups.heading: Earthworks and site development

groups.heading: Drainage and erosion control

name: Electrical Engineering
shortSummary: Power, instrumentation, metering and electrical installations.
summary: Electrical installation, instrumentation and metering for buildings, water schemes and industrial sites.

intro: Sato was founded by an electrical engineer, and electrical work runs through the firm's project record — from the pump control and high lift installations on water supply schemes to the supply and installation of bulk and prepayment metering for utilities and development programmes.
We deliver electrical works as part of a wider contract or as a package in their own right, and we commission what we install.

Electrical work is what turns a completed structure into an operating asset. It is specified against the duty of the plant it serves rather than against a catalogue, and it is tested and handed over as working plant.

Pump control panels and motor control centres
Supply, installation and commissioning of bulk, prepayment and electromagnetic meters
Solar power systems, including solar-powered borehole installations

groups.heading: Pump control and motor control centres
description: Control panels, starters and protection for water supply and pumping stations, built to the duty of the plant rather than to a standard schedule.

groups.heading: Metering supply and installation
description: Bulk, electromagnetic and prepayment meters supplied, installed, commissioned and handed over, with training for the staff who will read and maintain them.

groups.heading: Solar and standby power

groups.heading: Instrumentation and control

name: Mechanical Engineering
shortSummary: Pumps, pipework, plant installation and mechanical maintenance.
summary: Mechanical installation and maintenance for water, building services and plant.

intro: Sato's mechanical work sits alongside its civil and water engineering: pump houses, high lift pump installation, pipework and the plant that keeps a scheme running. The firm maintains its own fleet and workshop, which is where much of this capability was built.
We take on mechanical packages within our own contracts and as standalone installation and maintenance work.
Mechanical work is the moving half of an infrastructure contract. A pump house is a civil structure, a mechanical installation and an electrical panel at once, and it is sequenced as one job.

Pumping station and pump house mechanical fit-out
Planned and corrective maintenance of plant and equipment

name: Water Resources Development & Management
shortSummary: Dams, water supply, boreholes, river works, drainage and erosion control.
summary: Dams, water supply, boreholes and river works, with the drainage, flood and erosion control that protects them.

intro: Water infrastructure has been central to Sato's work for decades, with clients including the Ogun-Osun River Basin Development Authority, state water corporations, the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and the World Bank.
Flood and erosion control, river training, drainage and groundwater development are delivered by the same teams, because on most of these schemes they are one job.
Water is the infrastructure type that draws on all four disciplines at once. A scheme is treated as one job from source to tap, rather than as a civil contract with other trades attached to it.
items: Water supply scheme construction and rehabilitation, including intake structures and pump houses
Borehole drilling, including solar-powered boreholes, with our own drilling rig

caseStudy.heading: Well intervention strategies for production enhancement
caseStudy.challenge: A national oil company needed to increase production from mature brownfields at a profitable cost, but conventional workflows could not identify and rank intervention candidates across thousands of wells quickly, or predict post-job performance reliably.
caseStudy.solution: An automated production enhancement system covering candidate identification and ranking, AI-driven prediction of post-job well performance, and closed-loop evaluation of job outcomes.
caseStudy.resultsIntro: Validated in two giant brownfields with more than 3,000 active well strings and over 1,400 workovers a year.
results: Over 80% predictive accuracy in blind tests
5–20× more feasible high-value opportunities than manual review
250,000 barrels of oil per day of incremental production
17% less CAPEX to achieve the production uplift

name: Digitalization & Digital Twin Services
shortSummary: Asset data, analytics and virtual models of physical infrastructure.
summary: Turning asset data into a working digital model that operators can plan and maintain from.

intro: A digital twin is a model of a physical asset that is kept true to it: built from the asset's own drawings, instrumentation and operating records, and accurate enough that a change can be tested on the model before it is made on the plant. Used well, it turns a small number of measurement points into a picture of the whole system.

Sato approaches this from the infrastructure side. We already supply, install and commission the metering and instrumentation such a model depends on, and we already hold the asset records — drawings, as-builts, inspection histories — that give it something to be built from. The modelling and simulation are delivered with our technical partners.
This page describes a capability. Sato has no completed digital twin project to cite yet, and delivered work will be described here as it is finished.

items.name: Capture and structuring of asset records: drawings, as-builts, inspection and maintenance histories
Information management standards and workflows, so a model can be kept current rather than rebuilt
Digitalisation of paper maintenance, inspection and commissioning records
Field instrumentation, metering and telemetry specified and installed to feed an asset model
Integration with existing metering, SCADA and utility billing data
Condition and performance dashboards for the people operating the asset
Physics-based and data-driven models of structures, plant and process systems
Virtual testing of operating changes, uprating and modifications before they are made
Model validation against measured behaviour, and re-validation as the asset changes
Reservoir, well and production digital twins for oil and gas assets

intro: What a maintained model is actually for. Each of these is a decision an operator has to make anyway; the twin changes what it is made on.

groups.heading: Condition monitoring from a few sensors
description: A model calibrated against measurement infers what is happening across a structure or a system from the handful of points where instrumenting it is practical. That is usually the difference between monitoring an asset and instrumenting all of it.

groups.heading: Maintenance planned on evidence
description: Inspection and intervention planned against what the measurements and the model say about condition, rather than against a fixed calendar that is either too early or too late.

groups.heading: Testing a change before it is made
description: Operating changes, modifications and uprating tried on the model first, where being wrong costs nothing and where the answer arrives before the shutdown is booked.

groups.heading: Real-time production optimization
description: For oil and gas assets, the real-time optimization, AI-assisted production and reservoir work set out under Oil & Gas Services, delivered with the same partner team. The solutions stack there — surveillance, analysis, optimization, transformation — is the same one applied to a producing field.
groups.linkLabel: The oil and gas solutions stack

groups.heading: Metering data and water accounting
description: Bulk and consumer metering brought together so a water undertaking can see where water and revenue are being lost. Sato has supplied and installed metering at that scale; the analysis built on top of it is what is new.

intro: Sato delivers digitalization and digital twin work with its technical partners. The modelling, simulation and data science sit with them; the asset knowledge, the instrumentation and the site delivery sit with us.
It is the same technical partner team that delivers Sato's oil and gas services.

name: Research, Technology & Innovation Services
shortSummary: Applied studies, technical training and new engineering methods.
summary: Applied research, technical training and the evaluation of new methods and technologies.

intro: Research here means answering a question a project cannot proceed without: whether a method will work on this ground, whether a technology is worth adopting, what a material really costs across its life. It is applied work with a decision at the end of it.
Sato invests in the technical development of its own people and, with its technical partners, in studies that test a method or a technology before it is committed to on a contract.
This division is new. It is offered as a capability rather than as a record of completed research, and its scope will be described more precisely as work is delivered.

Evaluation of new materials, methods and construction techniques against site conditions
Cost engineering, estimation and whole-life cost comparison
Numerical modelling and simulation applied to a specific engineering question
Small analysis tools built for a workflow that no product covers
Assessment of software and analysis platforms before a team commits to one
Technical training for client and contractor teams, on the plant and systems they will operate
Petro-technical and facility management training
Knowledge transfer built into project delivery rather than bolted on at handover

groups.heading: Method and technology evaluation
description: A defined question, a method for answering it, and a recommendation the client can act on or reject. Scoped so the cost of the study stays small against the cost of getting the decision wrong.

groups.heading: Engineering analysis on demand

groups.heading: Custom analysis tooling

groups.heading: Training programmes

intro: Sato delivers research, technology and innovation work with its technical partners. The applied research and computational capability sit with them; the engineering question, the site and the project context sit with us.
